historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_driven_decelerating (management guide + FY2025 actual +14%, Q1-2026 +8% breach-impacted, Q2-2026 guide +9-10% cc)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (24.2%, 3yr) and revenue CAGR (18.8%, 3yr) are not meaningful as growth drivers here: FY2020 equity was negative (post-IPO recap distortion) so a clean 5yr equity CAGR cannot be computed, EPS CAGR is not meaningful given a 2023 net-income spike from a one-off tax benefit followed by declines, and FCF CAGR is negative/not meaningful because FCF swung from -$1,082M (FY2021) to a $1,775M peak (FY2023, inflated by working-capital tailwinds) down to $527M (FY2025) and -$110M (Q1-2026, data-breach compensation). Given this volatility, the model uses a revenue-driven, decelerating growth path (FY2025 revenue +14%, Q1-2026 +8%, Q2-2026 guided +9-10% cc) combined with an FCF margin that normalizes from the FY2025 trough (1.5%) toward 3.5% mid-term, rather than compounding any single historical CAGR.

base.notes: WACC includes ~+1pp regulatory/litigation risk premium for ongoing PIPC/KFTC matters and breach-related securities litigation. FCF margin normalizes from FY2025's depressed 1.5% (capex ramp + breach costs) toward 3.5% by Y3-5, versus FY2024's 3.4% and FY2023's inflated 7.3%.

bull.notes: Breach fully recovered (WOW membership restoration continues past the ~80% already recovered by April 2026), ads + Eats + Taiwan profitability inflect, Product Commerce adj. EBITDA margin (~8.4%) increasingly converts to FCF.

bear.notes: Breach-driven churn persists longer than management's April-2026 recovery claim, KFTC imposes structural remedies (Eats unbundling, search-ranking corrective orders), and AliExpress/Temu continue Korean share gains, keeping FCF margin structurally near 2%.

valuation.notes: Current EV/FCF is ~45x on FY2025 FCF ($527M) and even higher on TTM FCF (~$301M) because trailing FCF is trough-distorted by the data-breach compensation program and Taiwan/automation capex ramp. All three scenarios' implied exit multiples (9.7x-13.7x) are well BELOW this trough-distorted current multiple, so the model is not assuming multiple expansion versus today's reported EV/FCF -- the apparent 'compression' simply reflects FCF normalizing higher off a depressed base, which is the intended effect of the margin-normalization assumption.

historical_averages_ex_outliers.pe_note: P/E not a meaningful anchor: NI near zero makes trailing P/E 214-275x in FY2024-25; FY2023 21.6x inflated by one-off $895M tax valuation-allowance release

sanity_check.diagnosis: No fix needed. Base IV $11.54 implies EV/AdjEBITDA 11.0x vs 24.8x historical average and P/Sales 0.61x vs 1.26x historical average — the model values CPNG BELOW every multiple the market has historically paid. Base-case upside is negative (-25.5%), price sits at the 9th percentile of the post-IPO range, and implied exit multiples (9.7-13.7x TV/FCF5) assume no multiple expansion.
sanity_check.note: Sanity check guards against DCF over-valuation; this model errs conservative. The market's 1.26x average P/Sales would imply ~$24/share on FY2025 revenue — the DCF's discount reflects the breach fallout, regulatory fines, and FCF-margin uncertainty.
